papers.title: Integrating niches of the pathogen, multiple host and vector species highlights abiotic constraints and host‐vector interactions shaping pine wilt disease risk in China
papers.authors: Wang Wen-quan, Ting Du, Jiangxia Ye, Xiaohong Huang, Yangyang Li
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Pine wilt disease (PWD), caused by Bursaphelenchus xylophilus (PWN), is a major threat to forest health and pest management in China. Because PWD results from interactions among the pathogen, vector insects, and host plants, single-component analyses may misrepresent disease risk and overlook species-specific contributions. We integrated the environmental niches of the pathogen, hosts, and vectors to characterize abiotic constraints and biotic influences on PWD risk, quantify species-specific contributions and interactions, and inform surveillance priorities. RESULTS: Ensemble ecological niche models were developed for PWN, 17 susceptible hosts, and 10 potential cerambycid vectors across China and integrated with GeoDetector analysis. Although suitability patterns were broadly consistent, PWN had a much narrower suitable range than hosts and vectors, and this concordance declined under future climate scenarios. Bioclimatic variables were the primary determinants of habitat suitability for most species, whereas PWN showed narrower optimal ranges for key environmental drivers than most hosts and vectors. papers.title: A model for the spatial population dynamics of the European invasion of the Japanese beetle (Popillia japonica)
papers.authors: Davide Martinetti, Laura Erbetta, Danièle Bevacqua, Olivier Bonnefon, Marino Gatto
papers.abstract: Popillia japonica is an invasive beetle first detected in Northern Italy in 2014 and considered as one of the most dangerous pests for crops due to the economic, environmental, and social costs by European phytosanitary authorities. Here we develop a process-based model for quantifying the invasion dynamics of P. japonica with the goal to elaborate risk maps for the design of surveillance and control strategies. The proposed spatially heterogeneous model captures the different behaviors of both adults, which drive the invasion through flight and short-distance human-mediated transport, and ovo-larval stages, which affect demography due to their susceptibility to environmental conditions. Both processes are biologically informed through variables that are known to influence population dynamics, namely the number of summer days, affecting the flight ability of the adults, and the environmental suitability for larval survival. The simulated presence of adult beetles is then contrasted to pest observation data at the municipality scale from Northern Italy and Switzerland from the initial invasion to December 2023. papers.title: Citizen Science and Environmental DNA Reveals Site of an Invasive Paropsisterna beata (Newman) (Coleoptera: Chrysomelidae) Population in New Zealand
papers.authors: Toni M. Withers, Andrew R. Pugh, Darryl A. Herron, Dean Satchell, Shaun Wilkinson
papers.source: OpenAlex / New Zealand Journal of Zoology
papers.abstract: More than a decade after being declared eradicated, a population of the Australian blessed leaf beetle Paropsisterna beata (Coleoptera: Chrysomelidae) was located in New Zealand in 2026. The pest has been found and photographed three times by citizen scientists approximately 25 km north of the original Wellington infestation and reported on iNaturalist. An environmental DNA (eDNA) match from a water sample then directed searching to Eucalyptus trees visible on Google Earth upstream. This sequence of events leading to finding an established population highlights the potential for citizen science observations and eDNA monitoring to both uncover and pinpoint a cryptic pest's location as part of biosecurity surveillance.

papers.title: CRISPR/Cas biosensing for plant pathogens and engineered crops
papers.authors: Muhammad Ans Hussain1, Ihtisham Ul Haq, Sana Liaqat, Adeena Shakoor, Iqra Noor
papers.abstract: Plant pests (pathogens, insects and weeds together) remove up to 40% of global crop production every year, and plant diseases alone cost more than USD 220 billion, yet outside certification, quarantine and seed-testing schemes most infections are confirmed only after symptoms appear, when the epidemic has already outrun the intervention. Closing this lag requires assays combining reference-method specificity with a portable, instrument-light format. CRISPR/Cas biosensing addresses this requirement: once a Cas effector binds its programmed target, Cas12 and Cas13 enter a collateral trans -cleavage state that cleaves labeled reporters in large molar excess, converting sequence recognition into a fluorescent, colorimetric or lateral flow signal typically within 15 to 60 min and reaching attomolar sensitivity with pre-amplification. Depending on the ortholog, guide design and conditions, recognition can resolve single-nucleotide differences. This review traces the toolkit from genome editor to field diagnostic across two applications usually treated separately: detection of plant pathogens and pests, and surveillance of transgenic and genome-edited crops. papers.title: Predicting plant invasions and range shifts in an era of climate change
papers.authors: Matthew E. Fertakos
papers.abstract: The combined effects of invasive species and climate change have disastrous consequences on ecosystems, economies, and human health across the globe. As one of the driving forces behind modern extinctions, invasive plants outcompete native species, cause erosion, alter nutrient composition in soils, increase the prevalence of wildfires, as well as host and transmit pests and parasites. Meanwhile, rapid climate change is outpacing the ability of some native plant species to shift their ranges through natural dispersal. My dissertation explores how and why plants become invasive, solutions we can implement to improve prevention and slow their spread, and how we can restore and conserve species already negatively impacted by invasions. One of the main introduction pathways for invasive plants is the ornamental plant trade. For centuries, non-native plants have been transported from overseas to be bought and sold outside of their native ranges, some of which have escaped cultivation, established in the natural landscape, and subsequently become invasive. papers.title: Potential exposure risk of global timber production, carbon stocking, and biodiversity to forest pests
papers.authors: Yuxin Qiao, Jianquan Liu, David P. Edwards
papers.abstract: Abstract Pests pose escalating threats to forest ecosystem services globally, yet the patterns of forest vulnerability to these threats remain unclear. Leveraging over 7 million occurrence records of 1875 pest species, we identify northwestern Europe and eastern North America as global epicenters of forest-pest richness, dominated by insect fauna. Potential risk zones where timber production, carbon-rich forests, or diverse tree communities are exposed to high pest richness within and outside host native ranges cover 3.5% and 1.6% of forest globally, respectively. Forests in regions with stable temperatures, adequate precipitation, and high timber import volumes support high ecosystem services but also favor elevated pest richness, while forest fragmentation amplifies vulnerability to pests. Our findings provide a spatial blueprint for global pest management and underscore the urgent need for protecting forest health.

papers.title: Sources, Transmission, and Control of Salmonella in Vertically Integrated Broiler Chicken Production: Farm, Hatchery, and Processing Plant
papers.authors: Deepak Subedi, Bharath Mallavarapu, Pranita Patil, Abhisek Niraula, Milan Kandel
papers.source: OpenAlex / Comprehensive Reviews in Food Science and Food Safety
papers.abstract: Salmonella remains one of the most important foodborne pathogens associated with poultry products, despite substantial progress in processing hygiene and antimicrobial interventions. This review critically examines the sources, transmission routes, and control strategies for Salmonella in vertically integrated broiler production systems. Attention is given to contamination originating from breeder flocks, hatcheries, feed, water, litter, grow-out farms, transport, processing environments, and finished products. Preharvest interventions, including biosecurity, breeder and hatchery control, vaccination, litter and water management, feed hygiene, probiotics, prebiotics, organic acids, essential oils, bacteriophages, and bacteriocins, are evaluated according to mechanism, evidence strength, and commercial relevance. Postharvest interventions, including scalding, picking, evisceration control, chilling, peroxyacetic acid application, carcass rinses, post-chill treatments, and finished-product verification, are reviewed in relation to microbial reduction and process control. papers.title: Spatial targeting and expansion prevention offer effective pathways to protect African maize from parasitic weeds
papers.authors: Franck B.N. Tonle, Alcade Segnon, Mori W. Gouroubera, Dan Makumbi, Hugo De Groote
papers.abstract: Parasitic weeds (Striga spp.) threaten food security for over 300 million Africans dependent on maize, yet economic impact estimates vary widely due to high uncertainties, limiting strategic planning and interventions. We developed a spatially-explicit framework overcoming data scarcity through integrated agroecological similarity mapping, machine learning, and stochastic modeling to quantify Striga economic impacts across African maize production systems. Our analysis resolves decades of uncertainty, revealing annual losses of US$1.04 billion (95% confidence interval: US$0.94–1.15 billion) with high spatial concentration: less than 6% of infested areas generate half the economic losses. Agricultural expansion represents the primary future risk, potentially tripling losses by 2050 as Striga colonizes new areas. Interventions achieve maximum impact through a dual strategy: spatial targeting of high-loss zones coupled with prevention in agricultural expansion areas. This targeted approach outperforms uniform intensification, providing a blueprint for managing agricultural pests in data-scarce regions. papers.title: Sensitivity evaluation and multi-omics analysis of Bursaphelenchus xylophilus populations to emamectin benzoate in Shandong province field
papers.authors: Kunyang Ju, Zhifan Ma, Shuhan Guo, YuKe Wang, Shengnan Dong
papers.abstract: Pine trees provide substantial ecological and economic benefits worldwide, including water conservation, timber production, and carbon sequestration. However, Bursaphelenchus xylophilus , as the pathogen of pine wilt disease (PWD), results in extensive pine mortality annually, posing a serious threat to global pine resources and environmental security. Currently, chemical control remains the primary strategy for managing PWD. In Shandong Province, emamectin benzoate (EB) is the main nematicide for trunk injection. Nevertheless, long-term use of a single compound carries a high risk of resistance development. In this study, the sensitivity of 15 B. xylophilus strains from different regions of Shandong Province to EB was evaluated. The highest and lowest LC 50 values were observed in the PL (320.99 μg•mL -1 ) and CD strains (114.63 μg•mL -1 ), respectively, yielding a resistance ratio (PL vs CD) of 2.8 < 5, indicating that EB resistance may not have developed in the B. xylophilus populations in Shandong. papers.title: Prevention of Destructive Fishing in the Waters of Tual City: Effective Surveillance and Law Enforcement Strategies
papers.authors: Suharta ., Sigit Bintoro, Riyan Maulana, Ismi Isti Anah
papers.source: Crossref / International Journal of Multidisciplinary Research and Growth Evaluation
papers.abstract: <jats:p>Destructive fishing in the waters of Tual City remains a significant environmental and socio-economic issue, threatening marine biodiversity and the livelihoods of local fishermen. This study analyzes the problem using a SWOT approach, identifying strengths such as existing government regulations and rich marine resources, weaknesses including limited enforcement capacity and economic dependence on harmful fishing practices, opportunities such as growing global demand for sustainable seafood, and threats like illegal fishing and climate change. Based on the SWOT analysis, several policy recommendations are proposed, including strengthening law enforcement, promoting sustainable alternative livelihoods, enhancing education and awareness programs, expanding marine protected areas (MPAs), and creating market incentives for responsible fisheries. These strategies aim to transition Tual City towards sustainable fisheries management, balancing environmental conservation with economic development. Effective implementation of these policies will not only mitigate destructive fishing but also ensure long-term resilience for both the ecosystem and local fishing communities.</jats:p>

papers.title: Improved YOLOv26-ACearly-ASPPdeep for citrus disease and pest detection
papers.authors: Huiling Li, Xiaoxia Fang, Yufeng Shu, Yichun Zhan, Jiankai Chen
papers.abstract: This study addresses early and accurate detection of citrus diseases and pests under complex orchard conditions, which is essential for timely intervention and yield protection. Existing detectors often struggle with small lesions, subtle early symptoms, and cluttered foliage backgrounds. We propose YOLOv26-ACearly-ASPPdeep, a lightweight one-stage detector that functionally decouples feature enhancement across network depth: AdaptiveConv (ACearly) is embedded in shallow C3k2 blocks to strengthen fine-grained, content-aware filtering before aggressive downsampling, while ASPP-based multi-branch context aggregation (ASPPdeep) is placed in deep backbone/neck stages to enlarge receptive-field diversity for irregular lesion morphology. SCDown modules further reduce information loss during downsampling. Experiments on a Roboflow citrus disease/pest dataset (4,358 images; blackspot, canker, greening, and healthy) show that the proposed model improves max precision from 0.75565 (baseline YOLOv26) to 0.78032 (+3.26%) and raises mean Average Precision at IoU = 0.5 (mAP@0.5) from 0.791 to 0.863. papers.title: Risk-efficient Optimization of Cassava-based Cropping Systems Among Smallholder Farmers in Southeast Nigeria
papers.authors: Donatus Onwuha ONU, KC Igwe, MU Ozor, Temple Nwankwo, CO Odo
papers.source: OpenAlex / African Journal of Food Agriculture Nutrition and Development
papers.abstract: Cassava-based cropping systems are a vital component of smallholder agriculture in Southeast Nigeria, where farmers commonly cultivate cassava alongside other staple crops to enhance food security, diversify income, and reduce production risks. Despite the widespread adoption of mixed cropping, the selection of enterprise combinations is often based on traditional practices and immediate consumption needs rather than systematic economic analysis. Consequently, limited farm resources such as land, labour, and capital may be inefficiently allocated, resulting in reduced productivity and unstable incomes. Furthermore, farmers operate under significant uncertainties arising from climatic variability, pest infestations, fluctuating input costs, and unstable output markets. Identifying optimal and risk-efficient enterprise combinations is therefore essential for improving farm income and strengthening system resilience. This study analyzed optimal and risk-efficient enterprise combinations among cassava-based food crop farmers in Southeast Nigeria. papers.title: Real-Time UAV scheduling under hazardous weather conditions using an integrated fuzzy logic and machine learning framework
papers.authors: Ahmad B. Alkhodre, Adnan Ahmed Abi Sen, Abdelouahab Abid, Nour Mahmoud Bahbouh, Adel Ben Mnaouer
papers.abstract: The use of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) in precision agriculture, specifically palm farm management, is perpetually challenged by dynamic and extreme weather. From sudden wind gusts and thermal stress to destructive regional events like sandstorms and flash floods, these hazards severely constrict operational windows. This paper proposes a robust, hybrid scheduling framework that integrates fuzzy logic inference with an ensemble of machine learning classifiers to enhance real-time UAV flight reliability. The primary novelty of this research lies not in a new mathematical paradigm, but in its specialized application: the holistic integration of region-specific agricultural hazards into a real-time, decision-fusion architecture. The framework classifies takeoff viability into three categories (SAFE, CAUTION, and UNSAFE) automatically issuing alerts to trigger preventative measures and preserve hardware. By leveraging both short-term farm datasets and a decade of historical weather records, the fuzzy logic component reacts to rapid environmental shifts while establishing safety baselines. papers.title: Digital twin forestry as an informatics framework integrating remote sensing ecosystem modelling and data assimilation
papers.authors: Niamjit Das, Kevin Andrew
papers.abstract: Forests are essential to the Earth system, regulating carbon, water, and biodiversity cycles while underpinning ecosystem resilience. Yet they face mounting pressures from climate and land-use change, requiring integrative informatics approaches that link high-resolution observations with advanced ecosystem models. This systematic review defines Digital Twin Forestry (DTF) as an emerging paradigm that continuously couples multisensor Earth Observation data with ecosystem models through data assimilation, enabling dynamic, uncertainty-aware forecasting and adaptive decision support. Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, we synthesized 57 peer-reviewed studies published between 2016 and 2025 that combined EO datasets with ecosystem modeling and assimilation frameworks. Demonstrated advances include CubeSat constellations, spaceborne LiDAR, UAV hyperspectral systems, and hybrid machine-learning surrogates. Data assimilation methods such as Ensemble Kalman Filters and Particle Filters serve as computational bridges between multi-temporal observations and dynamic model states. papers.abstract: The bark beetle Dendroctonus micans (Kug.) (Coleoptera, Curculionidae, Scolytinae), a pest of spruce and pine, probably originates from eastern Siberia. Its closest relative is the North American D. punctatus (LeConte), on the other side of the Behring Strait. D. micans has largely spread westward and is presently established in most of the spruce forests of Eurasia. In newly colonised territories, it is considered as a tree-killing pest. A very specific predator, Rhizophagus grandis (Coleoptera, Monotomidae), has followed its prey in its territorial expansion, with temporal and spatial lags due to long distance passive transportation of D. micans with trade, and to habitat fragmentation. When both species coexist, D. micans is very sparce and only occasionally kills trees, because the high capacity of R. grandis to locate prey even at very low densities enables it to control the pest. This very particular relationship has been exploited for biological control. papers.abstract: Pepper (Capsicum annuum L.) is a lucrative crop, but problems arise when it is cultivated intensively, such as soil-borne disease outbreaks, excessive chemical fertilization, and soil degradation, reducing pepper’s yield and quality. Here, we experimentally investigated how the biocontrol agent Bacillus subtilis affects pepper growth, disease incidence, fruit quality, soil physicochemical properties, and its rhizosphere microbial community. In plate confrontation assays, this strain has a strong antagonistic effect against Phytophthora capsici, a major plant pathogenic oomycete causing pepper blight, inhibiting its mycelial growth by 56%. Field experiments show that, compared with the fertilizer control group (CF+OF), adding a biocontrol agent (CF+OF+KC) significantly reduces disease incidence, to 3% (a 85.7% reduction). Notably, the activity of systematic host defense enzymes (PAL, PPO) was negatively associated with disease incidence. In response, pepper yield increased by 17%, while its vitamin C content—a key fruit quality indicator—was greatly enhanced, by 55.1%. This combination of environmental sensing, lightweight machine learning algorithms and actuation on microcontrollers enables the system to do real time, adaptive irrigation scheduling. Their implementation of important parts like Raspberry Pi 4 as an AI inference module and an STM32 microcontroller as an actuator controller accelerates the responsiveness, increases security, and saves energy consumption since there is no need in cloud computing. Using the local climatic and soil moisture data the machine learning model identifies optimum irrigation time and duration looking at various parameters such as temperature, humidity, rain and crop-specific thresholds. The whole decision-making process is automated and carried out at the edge that makes it functional even without interruption in areas with poor or no internet connection. papers.authors: Robert Ugochukwu Onyeneke, Chukwuemeka Chinonso Emenekwe, Chinedum Uzoma Nwajiuba

papers.abstract: Crop diversification is a climate-smart agriculture (CSA) practice with well-documented yield and agroecological benefits, but rigorous, nationally representative evidence on its welfare impacts in Nigeria remains scarce. This study examined the determinants and welfare effects of crop diversification adoption among 3,229 farm households, using the fourth wave of Nigeria’s Living Standard Measurement Study – Integrated Surveys on Agriculture (LSMS-ISA). A probit model identified the determinants of adoption, and an endogenous switching regression (ESR) model, which corrects for selection bias arising from observed and unobserved heterogeneity, estimated the causal impact of adoption on household per capita consumption expenditure and dietary diversity. About 1,846 households (57%) adopted crop diversification. Household size, farm size, age of household head, distance to road, fertilizer use, and temperature exposure significantly increased the probability of adoption, while education, distance to market, access to finance, and rainfall shock significantly reduced it. The bibliometric analysis revealed a significant increasing trend in year-wise publications and citations, wherein India and the US emerged as the leading contributors with total publications of 34 and 25 respectively. Notably, the systematic narrative review highlights that agro-advisory systems (AAS) have increased farmer income by 83 %, improved crop yields by 6–25 % and enhanced farm profitability by 15–26 % in India. Despite these achievements, conventional AAS frameworks that rely predominantly on automatic weather stations (AWS) continue to face critical limitations, including sparse spatial coverage, restricted agro-meteorological observations, data discontinuities and inadequate representation of local microclimatic variability. papers.abstract: Introduction Escherichia coli O157:H7 ( E. coli O157 ) poses a severe global health threat, particularly due to its ability to form recalcitrant biofilms and the paradoxical exacerbation of life‑threatening haemolytic uraemic syndrome by conventional antibiotics. This study identifies piceatannol as an effective agent that suppresses E. coli O157 biofilm formation in vitro and acts as an adjuvant to enhance antimicrobial efficacy. Methods The effects of piceatannol on biofilm formation, swarming motility, and exopolysaccharide (EPS) and protein production were evaluated in vitro . Pharmacological screening identified an effective combination with polymyxin B, which was validated in a murine infection model by assessing bacterial loads in visceral organs (liver and spleen), ileal villous morphology, and survival rates. Results Piceatannol suppressed biofilm formation by inhibiting swarming motility and reducing EPS and protein production, thereby weakening biofilm integrity and enhancing antimicrobial efficacy. papers.title: Improved RT-DETR-based detection and counting of shrimp in EK80 acoustic echogram images
papers.authors: Yanrui Qu, Sheng Chen, 薛瑞超, Siyuan Zheng
papers.abstract: Accurately detecting shrimp targets in EK80 acoustic echogram images is challenging due to their small size, high-density aggregation, and strong background clutter, which collectively hinder conventional object-detection models. To address these issues, we propose an enhanced detection framework based on RT-DETR. Our method introduces three key improvements: the integration of an Efficient Multi-Scale Attention (EMA) mechanism to strengthen feature representation, the addition of a dedicated P2 detection layer to better capture fine-grained information for small objects, and the adoption of a combined Focal Loss and Wise-IoU (WIoU) loss function to mitigate class imbalance and refine bounding-box regression. Experimental evaluations demonstrate that the improved model achieves a mean mAP@50 of 0.844 and a mean mAP@50–95 of 0.437, outperforming the baseline RT-DETR. Furthermore, by incorporating DeepSORT for multi-object tracking and identity association, the proposed system enables automated shrimp counting with an average accuracy of 83.32% across 10 video clips. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in enhancing detection, tracking, and enumeration

papers.abstract: Abstract. Boreal forests, essential for carbon sequestration and multiple ecosystem services, face increasing pressure from climate-induced water stress. This study investigates how increasing water limitation affects growth and intrinsic water-use efficiency (iWUE) in Scots pine (Pinus sylvestris L) and Norway spruce (Picea abies (L.) Karst) in southern Finland. We combined site-level tree-ring data on basal area increment (BAI) and carbon isotope discrimination (Δ13C) from three sites per species, representing contrasting soil moisture conditions (dry versus wet), with regional growth indices from the Finnish National Forest Inventory (NFI) spanning 1990–2022. Our results show that forests in southern Finland have become increasingly water-limited over the past decade. Site-level and NFI based growth decline post-2015 is pronounced in Norway spruce, indicating strong sensitivity to water limitation, while Scots pine exhibits only marginal reductions beginning around 2010. papers.abstract: Abstract Saproxylic beetles are a highly diverse group of tree‐associated insects that play key roles in forest ecosystem functioning, comprising both rare primeval relicts and taxa of economic importance in timber production. Morphological identification of these beetles remains challenging due to high similarity among species‐rich taxa and a number of taxonomic specialists. While European DNA barcode reference databases have expanded in recent years, they remain dominated by western and northern populations, leaving Central and Eastern European taxa heavily underrepresented. Because previous studies have revealed pronounced east–west genetic divergence in several saproxylic beetle species, expanding barcode coverage in Central and Eastern Europe is highly necessary. Located within a biogeographical transition zone and harbouring some of Europe's last remnants of primeval forests, Poland represents a critical source of genetic data for these insects. papers.abstract: Before evolution can select anything, a physically possible causal architecture must already exist for selection to exploit. The T4 bacteriophage, a mindless nanoscale machine whose structure executes functions that map onto both empowering and disempowering strategies in Forde's framework of social dynamics, demonstrates this principle at the nanoscale. The strategies mapped include security, knowledge, hope, fairness, unity, and dignity, alongside their darker counterparts: nativism, hierarchy, misinformation, subjugation, dehumanization, and fear. Each concept is paired with a specific biological mechanism, virion stability, irreversible adsorption, superinfection exclusion, among others, showing that the mapping is grounded in observable structure. These mappings do not reify nonhuman organisms or attribute human qualities to mindless machines. They are structural descriptions: the concepts name functions that the architecture performs, not feelings that the organism experiences. papers.abstract: The materials of the XXXII International Symposium Bioinformatics and Computer-Aided Drug Discovery (Virtual, October 19–21, 2026) are presented. The Symposium is dedicated to addressing the emerging challenges and opportunities in in silicodrug discovery. It covers contemporary areas of biomedical science focused on analyzing normal and pathological states of the organism and elucidating pathological processes at the cellular and molecular levels. The main topics include the development and practical application of computational methods for identifying and validating new pharmacological targets, in silico design of potent and safe pharmaceutical agents, optimization of the structure and properties of drug-like compounds, and rational approaches to the use of pharmacotherapeutic agents in medical practice. This information will be valuable to researchers developing computational methods and applying them to drug research and development using bioinformatics and chemoinformatics approaches based on post-genomic technologies. It may also be of interest to undergraduate, graduate, and postgraduate students specializing in related fields.

papers.source: OpenAlex / Journal of the Botanical Research Institute of Texas
papers.abstract: This note presents the search for the type locality of the tepary bean, Phaseolus acutifolius. Two specimens kept in the herbaria of Harvard (GH00064068) and Kew (K000900693) were considered as lectotype and isolectotype, respectively. The field notes left by the collector Charles Wright and the analysis of the exploration conditions in October 1849 pointed to original collecting in the North Mountain of Hueco Tanks in El Paso County, Texas. During this study, the location was revisited in September 2025 and seed for germplasm conservation was collected. The role of the Texas Parks and Wildlife Department in saving a unique cultural and biological heritage is highlighted.

papers.authors: Letícia Alves, Janeide de Assis Guilherme Padilha, Phillip Joschka Haubrock, Amanda L. Subalusky, Ronaldo Sousa
papers.abstract: Non-native species are recognized as one of the major drivers of biodiversity change globally, with profound impacts on ecosystem functions and services. Despite the high number of studies on non-native species published, mainly in the last two decades, an often-overlooked aspect is their role as mediators of resource subsidies (the cross-boundary movement of energy, nutrients, or materials). This topic may have theoretical and empirical implications because non-native species may play a major role in ecosystem connectivity by transporting—or interrupting the transport of—energy and organic matter. Therefore, the main aims of this review were to (1) assess temporal trends, geographic distribution, and methodological approaches in research on resource subsidies mediated by non-native species; (2) synthesize how non-native species alter the magnitude, direction, and dynamics of resource subsidies across ecosystems and their implications for ecosystem functioning; and (3) identify key gaps in current knowledge and define future research priorities. papers.authors: Yian Li, Xiaoyu Guo, Hao Zhang, Jiayu Chen, Shuiwang Li
papers.abstract: Active visual perception enables an intelligent system to improve perception by controlling how visual evidence is acquired. However, differences in how studies define active perception and evaluate its benefits make approaches difficult to compare across tasks. This review first clarifies the field’s functional scope by examining whether an action is selected for its expected effect on subsequent visual evidence and whether the resulting observation informs a later decision. This definition distinguishes active observation acquisition from processing fixed inputs and guides the selection of representative literature. Within this scope, this review develops an analytical framework organized around four questions. It begins with what evidence the task requires, examines which actions can obtain that evidence and how a candidate observation should be valued, and considers how the next sensing action should be selected and executed. papers.title: Gıda Mühendisliğinde Güncel ve Arge Odaklı Araştırmalar
papers.abstract: Gıda mühendisliği, artan nüfus, değişen tüketici beklentileri, iklim krizi ve kaynakların sürdürülebilir kullanımı gibi küresel sorunlar karşısında yenilikçi çözümler üretmesi beklenen stratejik bir alandır. Gıda Mühendisliğinde Güncel ve Ar-Ge Odaklı Araştırmalar başlıklı bu kitap, alandaki güncel bilimsel çalışmaları ve teknolojik gelişmeleri disiplinler arası bir bakışla bir araya getirmektedir. Kitapta maydanozun (Petroselinum crispum) fitokimyasal profili ve gıda endüstrisindeki yenilikçi kullanım olanakları, gıda olarak farklı kullanım şekilleriyle, üzümden elde edilen ürünlerde kalite, güvenlik ve izlenebilirliğin sağlanmasında biyosensör teknolojilerindeki gelişmeler, yapay zekânın gıda kalitesi, üretim süreçleri ve sürdürülebilir gıda sistemleri üzerindeki dönüştürücü etkisi, interesterifiye yağların gıdalarda kullanımı, reaksiyonları, teknolojik avantajları ile sağlık üzerine etkileri konuları ele alınmaktadır. Bitkisel kaynaklı biyoaktif bileşenlerden ileri analiz ve dijital teknolojilere, yağ modifikasyonundan ürün geliştirmeye uzanan bu geniş yelpaze, gıda bilimindeki güncel yönelimlerin çok boyutlu yapısını yansıtmaktadır.
